question.worked_solution:
We use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{4}-1}\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x+x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{{e}^{4}-1}\frac{1}{1+x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)\,{|}_{0}^{{e}^{4}-1} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡[1+({e}^{4}-1)]-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+0) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{4})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1) \\  & =4-0 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
